The fourth: those who did not observe it with its proper observance are those who reached Muhammad (ﷺ) and did not believe in him. His saying: ﴿So We gave those of them who believed their reward﴾ means those who believed in Muhammad, and ﴿but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ means those who did not believe in him. What supports this is what is reported that he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in me, affirms me and follows me has observed it with its proper observance, and whoever does not believe in me, those are the ones who are destroyed."

The fifth: the righteous people among the folk of 'Isa (peace be upon him) initiated monasticism and passed away upon it. Then there came after them a people who followed them in words but not in deeds. These are the ones who did not observe it with its proper observance. 'Ata' said: "They did not observe it as the Disciples (*al-Hawariyyun*) observed it." Then He said: ﴿but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning that some of them undertook its observance, while many of them openly manifested disobedience and abandoned that path outwardly and inwardly.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and He will forgive you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Know that when He said in the first verse: ﴿So We gave those of them who believed﴾, meaning from the folk of 'Isa, ﴿their reward﴾, He said in this verse: ﴿O you who believe﴾, and the intended ones are those same people. He commanded them to fear God and believe in Muhammad (peace be upon him), then said: ﴿He will give you a double portion (*kiflayn*)﴾, meaning two shares of His mercy, for your believing first in 'Isa and second in Muhammad (peace be upon him). A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿They will be given their reward twice﴾ [al-Qasas: 54]. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning a people from among the People of the Book who came from Yemen to the Messenger and embraced Islam, so God gave them two rewards. Here there are two questions:

The first question: What is *al-kifl* linguistically? (Answer:) al-Mu'arrij said: *al-kifl* is "share" in the dialect of Hudhayl. Others said: rather, this is the language of the Abyssinians. Al-Mufaddal ibn Maslama said: *al-kifl* is a cloth which the rider wraps around the hump so that he can sit securely on the camel.

The second question: Since He gave them two portions and gave the believers one portion, their state would be greater (than that of the believers). (Answer:) It is reported that the People of the Book boasted on this account over the Muslims. But this is weak, because it is not far-fetched that one share might be greater in quantity than two shares. For if wealth is divided into two halves, one share is a half; and if it is divided into a hundred parts, one share is one hundredth. Thus one share from the first division is more than twenty shares from the second division. Likewise here.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and will appoint for you﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿a light by which you will walk﴾, which is the light mentioned in His saying: ﴿Their light running before them﴾ [al-Hadid: 12]. ﴿And He will forgive you﴾ what you committed of sins in the past. ﴿And God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿We did not prescribe it for them﴾, meaning We did not impose it on them.

As for His saying: ﴿except the seeking of God's good pleasure﴾, there are two views:

The first: it is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*, an exception where what follows is not of the same category as what precedes). The meaning is: "But they invented it, seeking God's good pleasure."

The second: it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*, an exception where what follows belongs to the same category as what precedes). The meaning is: "We did not impose it upon them except in the manner of seeking God's good pleasure." The intent is that it was not obligatory, for the purpose of performing an obligatory act is to avert punishment and attain God's pleasure, whereas the purpose of performing a recommended act is not to avert punishment, but rather its purpose is nothing other than attaining God's good pleasure.

As for God's saying: ﴿But they did not observe it with its proper observance. So We gave those of them who believed their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, there are several views:

The first: those who invented this monasticism (*rahbaniyyah*) did not observe it with its proper observance. Rather, they added to it the doctrine of the Trinity and incarnation. Some of them remained upon the religion of 'Isa (Jesus) until they reached Muhammad (ﷺ) and believed in him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So We gave those of them who believed their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾.

The second: We did not prescribe that monasticism for them except so that they might draw near to God's good pleasure by it. Then they did perform those acts, but not for this purpose; rather for another purpose, namely seeking worldly gain, ostentation and reputation.

The third: when We prescribed it for them, they abandoned it, and this would be a reproach to them insofar as they abandoned an obligation.

[Page 215]

The fourth: those who did not observe it with its proper observance are those who reached Muhammad (ﷺ) and did not believe in him. His saying: ﴿So We gave those of them who believed their reward﴾ means those who believed in Muhammad, and ﴿but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ means those who did not believe in him. What supports this is what is reported that he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in me, affirms me and follows me has observed it with its proper observance, and whoever does not believe in me, those are the ones who are destroyed."

The fifth: the righteous people among the folk of 'Isa (peace be upon him) initiated monasticism and passed away upon it. Then there came after them a people who followed them in words but not in deeds. These are the ones who did not observe it with its proper observance. 'Ata' said: "They did not observe it as the Disciples (*al-Hawariyyun*) observed it." Then He said: ﴿but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning that some of them undertook its observance, while many of them openly manifested disobedience and abandoned that path outwardly and inwardly.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and He will forgive you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Know that when He said in the first verse: ﴿So We gave those of them who believed﴾, meaning from the folk of 'Isa, ﴿their reward﴾, He said in this verse: ﴿O you who believe﴾, and the intended ones are those same people. He commanded them to fear God and believe in Muhammad (peace be upon him), then said: ﴿He will give you a double portion (*kiflayn*)﴾, meaning two shares of His mercy, for your believing first in 'Isa and second in Muhammad (peace be upon him). A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿They will be given their reward twice﴾ [al-Qasas: 54]. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning a people from among the People of the Book who came from Yemen to the Messenger and embraced Islam, so God gave them two rewards. Here there are two questions:

The first question: What is *al-kifl* linguistically? (Answer:) al-Mu'arrij said: *al-kifl* is "share" in the dialect of Hudhayl. Others said: rather, this is the language of the Abyssinians. Al-Mufaddal ibn Maslama said: *al-kifl* is a cloth which the rider wraps around the hump so that he can sit securely on the camel.

The second question: Since He gave them two portions and gave the believers one portion, their state would be greater (than that of the believers). (Answer:) It is reported that the People of the Book boasted on this account over the Muslims. But this is weak, because it is not far-fetched that one share might be greater in quantity than two shares. For if wealth is divided into two halves, one share is a half; and if it is divided into a hundred parts, one share is one hundredth. Thus one share from the first division is more than twenty shares from the second division. Likewise here.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and will appoint for you﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿a light by which you will walk﴾, which is the light mentioned in His saying: ﴿Their light running before them﴾ [al-Hadid: 12]. ﴿And He will forgive you﴾ what you committed of sins in the past. ﴿And God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 57, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of tremendous bounty﴾. In this there are two issues:

The first issue: al-Wahidi said: This is a difficult verse, and the exegetes have no clear statement regarding how this verse connects to what precedes it.

Know that most of the exegetes hold that "lā" (no) here is an extra particle (ṣila zāʾida), and the estimated reading is: "so that the People of the Book may know." Abu Muslim al-Isfahani and another group said: this word is not extra, and we will explain the verse according to both views, by the help and guidance of Allah, may He be exalted.

As for the well-known view, that this word is extra, know that it is necessary here to present an introduction, which is: the People of the Book, who are the Children of Israel, used to say: revelation and prophethood are among us, and the Book and the law belong only to us, and Allah, may He be exalted, has specially favoured us with this great virtue above all the worlds. Knowing this, we say: when He, may He be exalted, commanded the People of the Book to believe in Muhammad, peace be upon him, and promised them a great reward for that belief, He followed it with this verse, and its purpose is to remove from their hearts their belief that prophethood is restricted to them and is not found except among their people. So He said: We have only elaborated this explanation and extended the promise and warning so that the People of the Book may know that they have no power to restrict the bounty of Allah to specific peoples, and they cannot confine messengerhood and prophethood to particular peoples; and that bounty is in the hand of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills, and there is no objection to Him in that at all.

As for the second view, that the word "lā" is not extra: know that the pronoun in His saying ﴿ألّا يَقْدِرُونَ﴾ ("that they have no power") refers to the Messenger and his companions. The estimated meaning is: so that the People of the Book may know that the Prophet and the believers have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah; and if they do not know that they have no power over it, then they know that they do have power over it. Then He said: ﴿and that bounty is in the hand of Allah﴾, meaning: and so that they may know that bounty is in the hand of Allah. The estimate thus becomes: We did such and such so that the People of the Book do not believe they have power to confine the bounty and kindness of Allah to specific peoples, and so that they believe that bounty is in the hand of Allah. Know that this view has nothing in it except that we have supposed an addition in it, so we said in His saying ﴿وأنَّ الفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ﴾ the estimate: "and so that they believe that bounty is in the hand of Allah."

As for the first view, we needed to assume the deletion of something existent, and it is known that supposition (ʾiḍmār) is preferable to deletion (ḥadhf), because when the speech requires supposition, its apparent meaning does not give rise to falsehood at all; but when it requires deletion, its apparent meaning gives rise to falsehood. So we know that this view is preferable. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: The author of al-Kashshaf said: It has been read: "likay yaʿlama" (لِكَيْ يَعْلَمَ), "likaylā yaʿlama" (لِكَيْلا يَعْلَمَ), "liyaʿlama" (لِيَعْلَمَ), and "liʾan yaʿlama" (لِأنْ يَعْلَمَ) with the assimilation of the nūn into the yāʾ. Ibn Jinni related in al-Muhtasab from Qutrub that it was narrated from al-Hasan: "līlā" (لِيلا), with a kasra on the lām and a sukūn on the yāʾ. Ibn Mujahid related from him: "laylā" (لَيْلا), with a fatḥa on the lām and a jazm on the yāʾ without a hamza. Ibn Jinni said: What Qutrub mentioned is closer, because when the hamza is deleted, "līlā" remains, and the yāʾ must be assimilated into the lām, becoming "lillā"; the lāms then cluster, so the middle one is made a yāʾ because it is vowelless and the letter before it is kasra, becoming "līlā." As for Ibn Mujahid's transmission from him, the reasoning concerning it is that the lām of genitive, when you attach it to a pronoun, takes a fatḥa, you say "lahu" (لَهُ); so some people analogised the apparent noun to it. Abu Ubayda related that some of them read: (وإنْ كانَ مَكْرُهم لَتَزُولَ مِنهُ الجِبالُ) [Ibrahim: 46].

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and that bounty is in the hand of Allah﴾, meaning in His dominion and disposal; and "yad" (hand) is like the saying ﴿He gives it to whom He wills﴾, because He is capable and free in choice, acting according to choice. ﴿And Allah is the Lord of tremendous bounty﴾. The tremendous must have a great benefaction, and the purpose is to exalt the status of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in his prophethood, his law and his Book. And Allah knows best what is correct, and to Him is the return and the final destination. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his family and companions, and grant them peace.
